intro: The Retinoblastoma — Toronto Stage is a oncology scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Post-enucleation staging of retinoblastoma. It scores 1 criteria and interprets the total across 5 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in oncology
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 1 criteria: Extent of disease. Totals are then banded: 1 stage or more - Stage 0: stage 0 - eye-preserving therapy (systemic/intra-arterial chemotherapy, focal therapy). Excellent survival in high-income settings; 2 stage or more - Stage I: stage I - completely resected after enucleation. Usually no adjuvant therapy unless high-risk histology; 3 stage or more - Stage II: stage II - microscopic residual disease. Adjuvant chemotherapy indicated; 4 stage or more - Stage III: stage III - regional extension. Intensive chemotherapy plus orbital radiotherapy; 5 stage or more - Stage IV: stage IV - metastatic. High-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue; CNS disease carries a very poor prognosis.
guidelineRefs: Source: Gupta S, Aitken JF, Bartels U et al. Paediatric cancer stage in population-based cancer registries: the Toronto consensus principles and guidelines. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:e163-72.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the Retinoblastoma — Toronto Stage use?
What do the bands of the Retinoblastoma — Toronto Stage mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: 1 stage or more - Stage 0: stage 0 - eye-preserving therapy (systemic/intra-arterial chemotherapy, focal therapy). Excellent survival in high-income settings; 2 stage or more - Stage I: stage I - completely resected after enucleation. Usually no adjuvant therapy unless high-risk histology; 3 stage or more - Stage II: stage II - microscopic residual disease. Adjuvant chemotherapy indicated; 4 stage or more - Stage III: stage III - regional extension. Intensive chemotherapy plus orbital radiotherapy; 5 stage or more - Stage IV: stage IV - metastatic. High-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue; CNS disease carries a very poor prognosis.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.
